title: Hannah's song (1 Samuel 2:1–10)
hookLine: "He raiseth up the poor out of the dust"

lines: THE BOY IS BROUGHT TO SHILOH.
cards: Hannah brings her son back up to Shiloh. He has been born and weaned, and she leaves him with the same priest to serve, as she promised. Last time, nobody could hear her.
This time the text gives us every word. "And Hannah prayed, and said," and what comes out is not a thank-you note. It's a song about the whole world turning over.
The mighty fall. The hungry eat. And at its center, one line about where God goes looking for people: "He raiseth up the poor out of the dust."

teach.h: MY HEART EXULTETH IN THE LORD.
teach.b: It starts with her: "My heart exulteth in the LORD." She has been mocked every year by someone with more; now she says her mouth is enlarged over her enemies. Then, almost at once, it stops being about her.

teach.h: THE MIGHTY FALL, THE HUNGRY EAT.
teach.b: The bows of the mighty are broken, and those who stumbled are girded with strength. Those who were full hire themselves out for bread, and the hungry cease to hunger.
"The LORD maketh poor, and maketh rich; He bringeth low, He also lifteth up." One woman's answered prayer, read as a pattern for everyone.
Then the center: "He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, He lifteth up the needy from the dung-hill." The lowest places the song can name.
And the next words say why: to set them among princes, to make them inherit a seat of honor. Not just rescued. Seated.
A psalm says nearly the same words. One more surprise at the end. The song closes with God giving strength to his king and exalting the horn of his anointed.
A king. Two days ago, Judges ended with no king in Israel.

teach.h: SHE SINGS OF A KING BEFORE THERE IS ONE.
teach.b: Hannah sings about a king who doesn't exist yet, and her son, the boy she just handed over, will be the one who anoints him.

teach.h: HE RAISETH UP THE POOR OUT OF THE DUST.
teach.b: Some readers hear the whole book of Samuel folded up inside her song.

how: Jews read Hannah's song as part of the book of Samuel, among the Prophets; by tradition her story is also read aloud in the synagogue on Rosh Hashanah.

o: a lullaby Hannah sang over her newborn son at night
a prayer of reversals: the low raised, the mighty fallen
a lament Hannah sang each year when Peninnah mocked her

s: Hannah's song is only about her own son
it starts with her, then sings of the whole world turned over: the mighty fall, the low are lifted.
the song mentions a king before Israel has one
it ends with strength for God's king and his anointed, while Judges ended with no king in Israel.
in the song God lifts the poor and leaves them by the road
the next words say why they're raised: to sit among princes.

games.q: you're Hannah. after years of waiting you finally had a son, and now you've brought him to Shiloh as you promised. what do you do?
o: leave him quietly and go home.
sing out a prayer about God turning the whole world over.
ask Eli to promise he'll be a great man.
games.why: and Hannah prayed, and said: my heart exulteth in the LORD. her private thanks becomes a song about the mighty falling and the poor being raised.

practice: Bring to mind one person who's low right now, lonely, broke, ignored, left out of the room, and picture where they're sitting. Then ask the song's question: what would it take, not just to help them up, but to give them a seat?
If you pray, hold Hannah's line for them: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust.

wordCard.voice: Hannah's song. The prayer Hannah sings at Shiloh when she gives her son to serve: the mighty fall, the low are raised and seated with princes. It closes a week that ran from the last judges to the first pages of Samuel.

orig.note: Hebrew: dust, the word in 'He raiseth up the poor out of the dust.'

carryVoice: Your line: raised from the dust. Not just a hand up, but a seat. That's the week.
